facts.statement: Vagaceratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Alberta.
facts.quote: Vagaceratops (meaning "wandering (vagus, Latin) horned face", in reference to its close relationship with Kosmoceratops from Utah) is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur which lived during the Late Cretaceous period (late Campanian) in what is now Alberta.

facts.statement: Vagaceratops was a medium-sized ceratopsian reaching 4.5 meters in length and weighing 1.2 metric tons.
facts.quote: Vagaceratops was a medium-sized ceratopsian, reaching 4.5 m in length and weighing 1.2 MT.

facts.statement: The genus is known primarily from three fossil skulls.
facts.quote: It is known primarily from three fossil skulls.

facts.statement: Fossils of Vagaceratops have been recovered from the Upper Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been recovered from the Upper Dinosaur Park Formation.

facts.statement: The relationships of Vagaceratops remain debated, with it having been allied variously with Kosmoceratops or Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: Its relationships remain debated. Vagaceratops has variously been allied with Kosmoceratops or with Chasmosaurus.

facts.statement: Vagaceratops lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Vagaceratops is classified in the family Ceratopsidae and the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
Fossil remains of Vagaceratops come from the Canadian province of Alberta, found in the upper part of the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles provienen de la provincia canadiense de Alberta, encontrados en la parte superior de la Formación Dinosaur Park.

facts.statement: It has been hypothesized that Vagaceratops was the last member of the Chasmosaurus clade from northern Laramidia, with its close relative Kosmoceratops being the last representative of the clade.
facts.quote: Se planteó la hipótesis de que Vagaceratops era el último miembro del clado Chasmosaurus del norte de Laramidia, siendo el último representante del clado su pariente cercano Kosmoceratops.
